hook: SCP-507 is a light read with a dark edge: an ordinary, slightly smug man who keeps slipping into other realities with no warning. Expect a character piece more than a monster file. Most of the fun comes from watching Foundation paperwork bend around someone who is basically a cooperative, mildly annoying houseguest.
whyItMatters: It's one of the early wiki's best-liked humanoid Safes, and its list of self-chosen nicknames is memorable enough that the page carries a 'grabnok' tag. The entry also name-drops several other objects in passing. That casual cross-referencing helped the early series feel like a shared workplace instead of a stack of unrelated reports.
thingsToNotice:
The travel log works because every trip is summed up by what 507 asks for once it gets back: a flashlight, antifungal drugs, a pistol loaded with rubber rounds. Those requests turn each horror into deadpan comedy, so the one trip that ends with no request at all lands with real weight. The Smiling Man's greeting implies 507 is already known over there, and the file never explains it.

Meanwhile the procedures hide a genuine threat in plain sight. The two-week rule about touching him exists because somebody already got lost.

related.note: The sapient object 507 pleaded to visit on a short trip.
